name: Mullo

attributes.attribute: a god of the continental Celts set beside Mars by Rome
a name that may mean mule or wall, a point not settled
a ram-headed snake in his images, a sign of healing

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mullo is a god of the continental Celts. The Romans set his name beside their war god, Mars. The word Mullo is far from clear. Some read it as mule, some as wall, and honest judges cannot agree which is right or what that root would call into the story. Some images show him with a ram-headed snake. That sign the Celtic world took as a mark of healing. Mullo, then, may be a healer whom the Roman eye saw in the cloak of a war god.
